newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Daewoo plans $500 mln LatAm investment.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo plans $500 mln LatAm investment.

text.p: South Korean Daewoo Electronics Co plans to invest $500 million in Latin America by 2000 and use its recently created Brazilian operations as an export base for the region, a company spokeswoman said.
The company also plans to open operations in Mexico and make the country its export base for Central and North American markets, she added.
Earlier this week, Daewoo formed a joint-venture with local electronic goods maker Cineral to produce microwaves, stereos, televisions and VCRs as of September.

Brazilian sales of electronic goods have been booming since the government implemented a successful antiinflation plan in-mid 1994, opening the market to millions of lower-income families. TV sales, for example, jumped 40 percent last year over 1995, said Cineral's President Abdo Hadade.
Daewoo would not disclose the amount of the investment in Brazil, but Hadade said Daewoo's alliance with Cineral would double the Brazilian firm's sales to $115 million this year.
Currently, Cineral has 2.8 percent of the country's electronic goods market but it plans to increase its share to 10 percent by 2000 with the joint-venture.
